verses.1: Having heard Rama's words, Lakshmana, the destroyer of enemy heroes, spoke with folded hands to the radiant Rama.
verses.2: O Kakutstha, how did those two, the Brahmin and the king, who had cast off their bodies and were honored by the gods, attain union with a body again?
verses.3: Rama, the greatly effulgent best among men and descendant of Ikshvaku, thus replied to Lakshmana who had spoken to him.
verses.4: Those two righteous ones, the king and the brahmin sage, having abandoned their bodies due to a mutual curse, became beings of air, their wealth being penance.
verses.5: The great sage Vasishtha, exceedingly greatly effulgent, being bodiless, went to his father's presence for the sake of another body.
verses.6: Then, he, the knower of dharma, having become air, saluted the feet of the god of gods, his grandfather (Brahma), and spoke these words.
verses.7: O Lord, O Lord of the worlds, O great god, I have attained a bodiless state due to Nimi's curse, and you yourself are born from an egg and a lotus.
verses.8: O Lord, great sorrow will befall all those without a body, as all actions are lost for one who lacks a physical form; therefore, you ought to grant the favor of another body.
verses.9: Then, Brahma, the self-born one of immeasurable splendor, said to him, "O greatly renowned one, enter the essence born of Mitra and Varuna."
verses.10: O best among twice-born, even there you will be born without a womb, and endowed with great righteousness, you will again return to my control.
verses.11: Thus spoken to by the god, and having saluted and circumambulated the grandfather Brahma, he quickly went to the abode of Varuna.
verses.12: At that very time, Mitra also performed the role of Varuna, accompanied by the Ocean of Milk and being worshipped by the best of gods.
verses.13: At that very time, Urvashi, the foremost Apsara, arrived at that place by chance, accompanied by her friends.
verses.14: Having seen her, beautiful and playing in Varuna's abode, great joy entered Varuna because of Urvashi.
verses.15: Varuna, seeing her with lotus-petal eyes and a face like the full moon, desired her, the best of Apsaras, for union.
verses.16: Then she, standing with folded hands, replied to Varuna, saying, "O Lord of gods, I have already been directly chosen by Mitra."
verses.17: Tormented by the arrows of Kama, Varuna then spoke, saying, "I shall discharge this semen into this pot made by the gods."
verses.18: O beautiful-hipped lady of excellent complexion, if you do not desire union, I shall thus abandon my desire for you and consider my wish fulfilled.
verses.19: Having heard those well-spoken words of Varuna, the protector of the world, Urvashi was extremely pleased and spoke.
verses.20: O lord, let it be so; my heart is indeed fixed on you, and my affection for you is great, but my body belongs to Mitra.
verses.21: Thus addressed by Urvashi, he indeed discharged that great and wonderful semen, resembling a burning flame of fire, into that pot.
verses.22: But Urvashi went to the place where the deity Mitra was, and Mitra, having approached her, spoke these words to Urvashi.
verses.23: Why did you abandon me, whom I had previously invited, and choose another husband; therefore, you are an ill-behaved woman.
verses.24: Due to this misdeed, you, sullied by my wrath, will reside in the human world for some time.
verses.25: Go today to Pururavas, the royal sage, son of Budha and king of Kashi, O ill-minded one, for he will be your husband.
verses.26: Then she, by the effect of the curse, went to Pururavas, the legitimate son of Budha, who had returned.
verses.27: Then to him was born a glorious and very powerful son named Ayus, whose son, Nahusha, became one with splendor equal to Indra.
verses.28: This refers to the one who ruled as Indra for a hundred thousand years when the actual Indra was agitated after casting his thunderbolt at Vritra.
verses.29: That Urvashi, with beautiful teeth, eyes, and eyebrows, then went to the earth due to that curse, resided there for many years, and returned to Indra's assembly upon the curse's expiration. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 56 ।। Thus ends the fifty-sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
